flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: d4 is not hanging. Bb7 attacks it and the queen recaptures, so taking on d4 loses a bishop for a pawn. The real idea is shutting the Owen bishop and grabbing space. Calling a space-gaining push 'saving a pawn' trains me to panic every time a piece stares at a defended pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to g7 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I fianchettoed. You sold me a relative pin of b2 to a1 that I will never use. Teach king safety, the long diagonal, and pressure toward the center. That pin is a detector toy, not a lesson.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your pawn to c6 puts it at risk of attack from the white d4-knight and pawn. A better move would have been moving your queen to c8.
flags.critique: c6 is not a loose pawn. Bb7 and Nd7 both defend it. dxc6 is a pawn fork of the bishop and knight, and the first capture is a pawn so the trade on c6 drops a pawn. That is the counting lesson. Qc8 is dumped with zero idea — unpin, prepare ...c5, get off the d-file? I cannot practice a SAN.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c6 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: It was defended twice. You win a pawn because you capture with a pawn first, then the c6 pawn forks Bb7 and Nd7. 'Undefended' is a lie, and doubled_pawns / passed_pawn in the reason list are my own c-pawns, not why the take is good.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c6 with your d4-knight is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended and it unveils an attack from your bishop on the black pawn.
flags.critique: Nd7 defends that bishop. Nxc6 forks the queen, and recapturing walks into Bxb6. That is why I do not take back. 'The black pawn' never names b6. You described a free piece that was not free and skipped the fork that actually wins the bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to d4 is the strongest move because it saves your d4-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The hanging knight is on c6. You labeled the destination and told me I saved a d4-knight that was not even there. I retreated a piece that just took on c6. Name the from-square, or I think you are talking about a different piece.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e4 with your f6-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your bishop on the white d4-knight.
flags.critique: Nc3 and Be2 both defend e4. I won a pawn by capturing with a second attacker, not by snacking on a loose pawn. The discovered Bg7 hit on Nd4 is real — lead with that and drop the 'undefended' lie.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your c3-knight is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: I recaptured a knight in the center. King safety is a leftover tag. Say I take back the piece. If you want a second idea, the e4-knight was staring at the kingside — not 'your king got safer' as the reason to recapture.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your knight is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn.
flags.critique: Be2 defends e4. This is the second recapture in the sequence, not a hanging knight. The discovered queen hit on c4 is the only true clause, and you still will not name the pawn. I am done believing 'undefended.'

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e4 with your f3-bishop is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and you take the defender of the black a8-rook.
flags.critique: Last move you said I pinned that knight to the rook. Now you pretend the knight was defending the rook. Knights do not defend a8 from e4. I took a pinned piece and the bishop now eyes a8. Teach pin exploitation, not a fake removed-defender.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and you take the defender of the white e3-bishop.
flags.critique: I recaptured a knight with a pawn. I am not a bishop ahead — White still has two bishops. Knights do not defend a diagonally adjacent bishop. The pawn on d4 now attacks Be3. That is a landing attack, not removing a defender. doubled_pawns and isolated_pawn are why the recapture is ugly, not why it is 'strongest.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your e3-bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Bg7 defends d4. The honest sentence is: the pawn was attacking your bishop, recapture. You had saves_piece in the reasons and still led with 'undefended.' Same recapture-is-a-tactic bug as dxc6 and Nxe4.

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to d8 is the strongest move because it saves your d8-rook from capture.
flags.critique: There was no rook on d8. Be4 was eating a8 — Bxa8 wins the exchange. I slid the rook off the bishop's diagonal. You labeled the destination again and hid the only tactic on the board.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on g7 with your d4-bishop is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black f8-rook.
flags.critique: Nobody is taking the f8-rook. I ripped the fianchetto to wreck the dark squares around the king. 'Defender of the f8-rook' is a trivia fact that sits next to the king. Teach the king, not a rook that is not hanging.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty verdict, 50cp swing, Owen Defense. I am preparing Bb7, not playing the engine's 'strongest' move. If you have no reason, do not crown it. At least say I am fianchettoing the queenside bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to b7 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: Every opening ply claims the center. Bb7 is the Owen bishop: long diagonal, pressure on e4. If you cannot say that, the because-clause is wallpaper.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Blank again. This is the other fianchetto, the one that actually happened next. 47cp and still 'That's the one.' Name Bg7 or I think g6 is just a random pawn nudge.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You tagged backward_pawn and then said nothing. c4 supports d5 and builds the big pawn center. I needed one concrete noun (d5, space, ...c5) and got a trophy.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Stops d5-d6 ideas, opens the bishop a crack, typical Modern/King's Indian shell. 'Strongest move' with an empty because is the same sentence as b6, g6, a6, and c4. I stopped reading it.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to c7 is the strongest move because it saves your queen from capture.
flags.critique: True that the c6-knight hits the queen, and you still will not say fork. Recapturing on c6 is legal; I skip it because Bxb6 comes next. Connect ply 19 to this instead of a lone 'save the queen' after you already claimed the bishop was free.

flags.quote: Moving your d7-knight to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Nc5 hits e4. That is the move. Empty strongest-move on the first real pressure of the game is malpractice. You have kicked_by_pawn in the stack — use it.

flags.quote: Castling kingside is the strongest move because it gets your king out of danger and activates your rook.
flags.critique: The castle sentence is fine. You also tagged ignored_threat and never mentioned e4. I just parked a knight on c5 hitting that pawn, then I take it next move. Tell me I am giving the pawn to get the king off e1 while still a piece up, or the threat tag is a lie.

flags.quote: Moving your a1-rook to c1 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Last ply you discovered the queen onto c4. Rc1 is the answer: defend the pawn. 75cp, blank because, 'That's the one.' The lesson was sitting in the previous sentence and you dropped it.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: e5 hits the d4-knight. You tagged ignored_threat and backward_pawn and used neither. Kick the knight, admit d6 becomes backward. Silence on a pawn contact move is how I learn nothing from a good move.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Reason: hanging. Copy: nothing. Is the queen leaving the c-file, supporting d6, or challenging Bd5? A hanging tag that never reaches the sentence is worse than no tag. I got a quip.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures undefended
suggestions.detail: wins_material fires when capturedSeeCp >= 80, then move-copy says 'the X was undefended' if SEE is near the piece value. dxc6, Nxc6, Nfxe4, Nxe4, Bxe4, and Bxd4 all got that lie on defended units. Gate wins_material on net material versus the pre-capture position, or suppress it when the captured unit is attacked by fewer than SEE-winning extra attackers. A 1200 who just recaptured will not trust the next hanging warning.

suggestions.title: Name the square you fled, not the landing square
suggestions.detail: retreatedToSafety pushes saves_piece with movedPiece.square = move.to, so labeledPiece emits 'd4-knight' and 'd8-rook' after Nd4 and Rad8. Pass move.from into that reason (or labeledPiece the before-FEN). Same bug twice in one game: I saved the c6-knight and the a8-rook. Destination labeling makes the sentence factually false.

suggestions.title: Require the captured unit to actually defend the target
suggestions.detail: detectRemovedDefender can fire when the captured piece does not attack newlyHanging (pin-line Ne4 vs a8, Nd4 vs Be3, Bg7 vs Rf8). Require namedAttackers(before, newlyHanging) to include the captured square, and require that newlyHanging is actually attacked after the move by a piece other than trivia adjacency. Pin captures should stay on the pin reason: you took the pinned piece, the bishop now eyes the rook.

suggestions.title: Do not call equal trades hanging
suggestions.detail: ...c6 was tagged hanging with two defenders; the lesson is a pawn fork plus capturing-first on a 2v2 square. Hanging should mean isHangingBySee, and pawn captures that fork two pieces need a fork reason (already in the stack) ranked above hanging. Naming Qc8 without a because is the same dump as other games: select-insight must spend suggestedBenefits on the alternative.

suggestions.title: Do not lead development with relative pawn pins
suggestions.detail: Bg7 led with pinning b2 to a1. relativePinsCreated on a fianchetto/development move should lose to development unless the pinned unit is a piece or the pin is absolute. Bd5 pinning f7 to the king is the good version — keep those. Club players will repeat the fake pin in their next game.

suggestions.title: If you tag ignored_threat, say what is hanging
suggestions.detail: O-O (e4), e5 (Nd4 / unused tags), Rc1 after the queen discovered onto c4, and Qd7 (hanging with no copy) all had threat reasons that never reached the sentence. When ignored_threat, kicked_by_pawn, or hanging is in pickBenefitReasons / pickProblemReasons, it must win the because-clause over silence or king_safer. Rc1 defending c4 was the cheapest win in this dump.

suggestions.title: Do not explain recaptures as king safety
suggestions.detail: Nxe4 (ply 27) and Bxc6 (king_safer in reasons) are captures. selectBecauseReasons already prefers tactics, but capture is then dropped because the playedPhrase already says 'taking,' and king_safer (90) fills the hole. If the played phrase is a capture, do not emit king_safer as the because. Recapture copy should be 'you take back' or the discovered-attack follow-up, never 'keeps your king safer.'

suggestions.title: Ban strongest-move with no because
suggestions.detail: b6, g6, c4, d6, a6, Nc5, Rc1, e5, Qd7, Nge2 are verdicts with empty or unused reasons. If benefit reasons are empty, fall back to a cheap fact already computed: pawn move that attacks a piece (kick), pawn move that defends a central pawn (c4 supports d5), knight developing toward a central outpost (Nge2-d4). 'That's the one.' on every best ply makes the quip unreadable by move 10.

whatWorked: Castling copy (plies 25 and 30) actually names king safety and rook activation.
Bxc6 (ply 18) correctly says the recapture saves the d7-knight from the c6 pawn.
Bf3 (ply 31) names a real pin of the knight to the rook — the one pin that paid off two moves later.
The discovered-attack clause on Nfxe4 (Bg7 vs Nd4) and Nxe4 (queen vs the c-pawn) is the right motif when it is not glued to 'undefended.'
c6 is at least called a blunder with named attackers; the classification matched Lichess even if the tactic was undersold.
